verdicts.summary: The 5s bound on the run-scope close holds. If a run-scope finalizer hangs, the finalizer still returns and markComplete fires. The unbounded steps before the close are already finding 0.
verdicts.scenario: Two pool instances are running and each run-scope finalizer hangs forever. The user quits. The scopedProgram finalizer runs stopAllPoolInstances. Each stop takes the mutex (free, no start in progress) and calls closeRun with a 5s timeout. closeRun forks Scope.close into the instance's parentScope (DesktopBackendManager.ts:648), which is still open because the program finalizer runs before the layers are torn down. Fiber.await is wrapped in timeoutOption and resolves to None after 5s. closed=false, so stop returns at 1088-1089. Effect.ensuring(markComplete) at DesktopApp.ts:336 then completes the Deferred that awaitComplete waits on (DesktopShutdown.ts:26-30, DesktopLifecycle.ts:93), and the .finally quit runs (DesktopLifecycle.ts:131-138). The process-kill grace is 2s (DesktopBackendManager.ts:67, 486), which is under the 5s budget, so a normal SIGTERM-then-SIGKILL teardown is not cut short. A hang in the mutex, onShutdown or the restart-fiber interrupt is still unbounded, which is finding 0.

verdicts.summary: The unbounded mutex wait while start holds it (configResolve, fs.exists, onPreflightFailed), plus the unbounded onShutdown and restart-fiber interrupt, is the hazard finding 0 already reports.
